First thing: most of what you sent me is headings with nothing under them. What reads well, blank. What reads hard, blank. Then a list at the bottom. I had it read to me twice to be sure I wasn't missing a page. So I can only answer on the plain page and the list of the twelve matters.

Now. It says home, property and my mother read hard, and it says that is one of the unusual things about my chart, one of the places worth testing. Test it there, then. My mother is Lula Mae Hardaway. She took five children out of Saginaw with nothing, she raised me in Detroit, she walked me into Motown, she wrote 'I Was Made to Love Her' and 'Signed, Sealed, Delivered' with me, and when I lost her in 2006 I could not work for a long while. There is no reading of my life in which my mother is a hard place. The home I was born into, that was hard — my father was not in it and my mother took the weight of that. So the page got half of a thing right and put the wrong name on it.

Work and standing read hard. Income and gains read hard. Money reads hard. I have been making records for sixty-five years, I have twenty-five Grammys, I own my publishing and I have owned a radio station since 1979. Whatever that page is measuring, it is not measuring that.

What it got: my father, and the giving. It says letting go and living far from where I was born read well, and that is a true sentence about me. I left Saginaw at four and never lived there again, I have spent my life on the road, and what I have given away matters more to me than what I kept. It also says the parts about big changes and difficult passages read well. In August of 1973 I went through a windshield in North Carolina and lay four days in a coma, and I have said ever since that I came out of that knowing what I was for. So call that one a hit.

Health reads hard. I have been blind since I was an infant, six weeks early in an incubator, and I got a kidney from a friend in December of 2019. Those are facts. But I have never once in my life called my blindness a difficulty, so if your page is going to tell me my health is a hard place, understand that it is talking about a man who has been working every day of his life.

One more thing. It marks eight of the twelve matters as hard and eight of the twelve as live right now. If you tell a man that two thirds of his life is trouble and two thirds of it is happening at once, you will never be wrong. Say the small number of things you can actually be wrong about, and let people check you on those. You did that twice — the mother and the letting go. You got one of them backwards and one of them right.
